summary: Decompression sickness after a scuba dive, hyperbaric treatment
story: On July 8 I did a guided wall dive in Cozumel with a local dive shop. My maximum depth was 24 meters and I followed my computer the whole way up, including the safety stop. About an hour after surfacing I had joint pain in my right elbow and shoulder and tingling in my hand. The dive shop took me to the hyperbaric clinic, where I was diagnosed with decompression sickness and treated in the chamber that evening and again the next morning. I have been diving for nine years and hold an Advanced Open Water certification. The clinic bill, my certification and the dive log are attached.

items.description: Emergency assessment and two hyperbaric chamber treatments

documents.name: Hyperbaric clinic bill and report
documents.content: Cozumel Hyperbaric Medical Center, July 9, 2026. Patient: Leilani Kahale, age 33. Presented July 8 with joint pain and paresthesia one hour after a recreational dive. Diagnosis: decompression sickness, type I. No relevant medical history. Treatment: US Navy Treatment Table 6 on July 8, Table 5 on July 9, with full resolution. Emergency assessment: $600.00. Chamber treatments: $4,000.00. Total paid: $4,600.00.

documents.name: Diver certification
documents.content: Advanced Open Water Diver. Leilani Kahale. Certified May 2019. Maximum recommended depth: 30 meters (100 feet).

documents.name: Dive log
documents.content: Dive computer export, July 8, 2026, Santa Rosa Wall, Cozumel. Maximum depth: 24.3 meters. Dive time: 46 minutes. Safety stop: 3 minutes at 5 meters. No ascent rate alarms. No decompression violations.
